description: Muni fare structure, fare-media mix, enrollment in discount/free programs, fare revenue per boarding, BART in-SF fares and the Clipper inter-agency transfer discount, compiled to decide whether the beta3 model should give a share of Muni riders a zero (or near-zero) marginal fare instead of charging every adult $2.85 per trip. All numbers are as printed in the named source unless a field is labelled 'derived' (arithmetic on sourced numbers) or 'uncertain'.

notes: Fiscal years end June 30 (FY2026 = FY25-26 = July 2025 - June 2026). NTD report year 2024 = SFMTA FY2024.

Fare capping does NOT exist on Muni as of 2026-10-05. The FY27-28 budget (approved 2026-04-21) adopts DAILY fare capping at two single-ride fares, 'targeted for Summer 2027' (approved-budget page; staff report lists it under FY27-28 changes effective Jan 3, 2028; news reports say 2028). An older 'monthly single ride fare capping' authorization was only a six-month MuniMobile pilot clause in the fare policy; no evidence it is in effect.
Clipper 2.0 (Next Generation Clipper, launched 2025-12-10) introduced tap-to-pay with bank cards and an MTC-funded inter-agency transfer discount of up to $2.85 within 120 minutes, not fare capping.

The 2025 Muni Onboard Survey (Spring 2024 - Winter 2025, >30,000 responses, >25,000 weekday) is the latest fare-media distribution. Its weighted total is 434,613 'estimated ridership' (weekday boardings expansion, presumably). Only fare media subject to the FY27/FY28 increases are itemised; free media (youth, Free Muni seniors/PWD, Access Pass) are not itemised and sit in the residual.

muniFares2026.source: sfmtaFaresPage (current) and fareTable2025 (effective 7/1/2025); confirmed unchanged through 2026-10-05 by the FY27-28 Title VI table 'FY26 fares'

adultSingleRide.note: Valid until 5 a.m. next day if bought after 8:30 p.m. (fareTable2025). Free transfers within the 120 min on Muni.

monthlyPasses.note: M/A valid for the calendar month plus until 11:59 p.m. on the 3rd of the next month on Muni; the A pass BART portion is valid within San Francisco only through the last day of the month (fareTable2025). Station range Embarcadero-Balboa Park per search snippet of BART/Clipper pages (uncertain).

freePrograms.youth: All youth 18 and under ride free (no card required except on cable cars); program 'Free Muni for All Youth'
freePrograms.seniorsAndPeopleWithDisabilities: Free for SF residents at/below 100% Bay Area Median Income (2026 limits: $109,100 for 1-person, $127,700 for 2, $155,850 for 4 household) - budgetStaffReportApr2026 Table 4
freePrograms.accessPass: Free for people experiencing homelessness certified by HSH
freePrograms.other: Uniformed SF police/sheriff, active SFMTA employees and some dependents/retirees (fareTable2025)

historyOfAdultClipperFare.uncertain: The Apr-2026 staff report text says the discount was reduced 'effective January 1, 2026, and July 1, 2026', which conflicts with the fare table (1/1/2025 and 7/1/2025); the fare table and fares page are taken as correct.

zeroMarginalFare_upperBound_passes+dayVi.note: Derived. Treats every residual response as zero-fare (free programs dominate it, but the staff report does not break it down). averageFarePerBoarding_derived.FY2024_note: NTD reports exactly $0.50/UPT for MB, TB, LR, SR - SFMTA appears to allocate non-cable-car fare revenue across modes by boardings, so mode differences are not meaningful.
averageFarePerBoarding_derived.FY2025_note: Numerator includes paratransit and citations; NTD 2025 annual fare revenue not yet in dataset.
averageFarePerBoarding_derived.FY2026_note: Q1 projection of revenue; visitor passes are also used on regular Muni so the split is approximate.
averageFarePerBoarding_derived.comparison: Model charges $2.85 per adult trip; observed revenue is ~$0.50-0.70 per boarding (all riders incl. free/discount/transfers/evasion).

consistencyCheck_derived.singleRide: FY26 single-ride revenue $74M / $2.85 = ~26.0M full-fare-equivalent paid fares/yr, while 54.8% of 175.0M boardings = ~95.9M boardings self-report pay-per-ride (2025 survey) - ~3.7 boardings per paid fare, more than 120-min transfers alone explain; consistent with substantial non-payment among self-reported single-ride riders (rough; senior/START fares are cheaper, so true paid fares are somewhat higher).
consistencyCheck_derived.monthly: FY26 monthly revenue $27M / $86 / 12 = ~26,200 M-pass-equivalents per month (more passes if the $43 discount passes are a large share).

officialEstimate.value: close to/just more than 20% of riders do not pay (vs 12% pre-pandemic on Muni Metro / 2019)
officialEstimate.source: chronicleEvasion2024 (headline) and GrowSF 2026-03-27 citing SFMTA; uncertain - methodology not published

may2026.value: about 1 in 4 riders not paying; 'approximately half of customers pay through invisible methods like apps or qualify as free riders'; 59 inspectors + 17 being added; ~$14M more rider revenue vs prior year

revenuePerRider.value: +6% Feb 2024 - Feb 2025 (controls for fare increases, excludes cable car)

freeMuniForYouth.participants: N/A (universal for 18 and under since 2021; no enrollment needed)
freeMuniForYouth.historical: 39,350 active users (~72% of eligible) when means-tested, per SFMTA 2021 blog (search snippet; uncertain)

bartInSF2026.source: bartFareApi (current fares, queried 2026-10-05); bartFareIncrease2026 (6.2% increase on 2026-01-01)
bartInSF2026.note: All tested trips between SF stations Embarcadero..Balboa Park cost the same $2.55 (the BART minimum fare in 2026). Crossing into San Mateo County (Daly City) jumps to $4.05.

transferDiscount.amount: up to $2.85 (the highest local single-ride fare on Clipper) off the second and later agencies within 120 minutes of first tap; unlimited transfers in the window
transferDiscount.start: 2025-12-10 (Next Generation Clipper; Clipper cards got it as they were upgraded over 8-12 weeks; bank cards immediately per BART)
transferDiscount.implication_derived: Per MTC/BART wording ('only charged full fare on the first operator'; discount up to $2.85 on each later agency, never below $0): Muni ($2.85) then BART-in-SF ($2.55) -> BART leg $0; BART-in-SF ($2.55) then Muni ($2.85) -> Muni leg $0 (discount $2.85 >= fare). A Muni+BART-in-SF trip within 120 min therefore costs one fare, the first operator's. Not available with MuniMobile (sfmtaFaresPage).
transferDiscount.status: MTC-funded pilot, to be reviewed in 18-24 months (search snippet; uncertain)
transferDiscount.previous: Before Dec 2025: $0.50 inter-agency discount to Muni (fareTable2025); free round trip transfer Daly City BART <-> Muni at that station.
